# Appendix II

*Pages PDF 34-45*

## **Appendix II Monsters and Npcs**
## **Alrik Okrisson Dwarf Bounty Hunter General**
Alrik is the angriest Dwarf in Skogholm, and possibly the entire Laurelorn forest. For centuries he’s tried – without success – to avenge his ancestors’ grudges from the War of the Beard. Alrik has apprehended some of the Laurelorn’s most notorious outlaws but catching Elves in the damnable forest is nigh impossible. They vanish before his crossbow can be reloaded, and they slip easily out of his manacles. A cheeky minstrel named Redfern has popularised songs depicting the bounty hunter as a buffoon. 

Forty years ago, an arthritic knee and failing eyesight forced Alrik into semi-retirement. Baron Nikse’s father Helmut approached the Dwarf with an offer. If Alrik recruited bounty hunters to rid the Forstmark of outlaws, the Nikse family would pay all bounties. Alrik accepted the baron’s deal, and within a week Elf convicts were being arrested by Alrik’s crew. Although many of the charges against Elves are spurious, the Nikse family continues sponsoring Alrik. 

Alrik is exceedingly polite to Elf characters because he wants to appear reasonable. He doesn’t belong to the Nordland Foresters’ Guild, but he admires Guildmaster Kochler and has helped the merchant spread rumours about Elves. 

Alrik has heard of the tainted wood north of Vesterrup but receives no compensation for bounties outside the Forstmark. Since the plague outbreak, Alrik has tried to arrest Redfern on charges of spreading the ‘fey curse’ through his music. Alrik currently resides in Forstfast as Skogholm is under quarantine.

## **Darlorhan, Lord of Shadows (Called ‘the Blinding Death’ by Dwarfs)**
The Elven archmage Darlorhan is over 4,000 years old. In the age before the War of the Beard, he lived as a hermit experimenting with Laurelorn’s exotic flora. Although Darlorhan’s reclusiveness earned him the epithet ‘The Hermit Lord’, he was one of the few wizards capable of binding departed Elven souls into trees to preserve them from Chaos. Darlorhan chose the site of Ammenvale for his work because it was shielded by an antiChaos field of ancient origin. 

During the later years of the War of the Beard, Darlorhan unleashed a deadly disease on the Dwarf invaders. In the Eonir’s hour of desperation, the mage had unknowingly struck a bargain with dark powers to complete his research. Today, Darlorhan’s body is preserved in crystal at Ammenvale, where the Shield of Asuryan is sustained by his magical essence. Though his body cannot move or speak, the Hermit Lord can still issue instructions to devoted guardians by means of telepathy. However, the voice they hear is actually Grubile the Inhabited, a greater daemon of Nurgle.

## **Torendil Redfern Wood Elf (Eonir) Minstrel**
Torendil is a famous personality in the eastern Laurelorn where he’s commonly known as ‘Redfern’. The young minstrel’s origins are as mysterious as his talent with a lute. No Elf is certain of his birth Kindred, only that he was born in Kor Immarmor and his grandmother was a famous mage in the War of the Beard. Redfern wanders the Laurelorn playing in Norland’s inns and gathering news of anything that might threaten the forest or his kin. 

At present, Redfern is hiding from Alrik’s bounty hunters in the Golden Wood. Though the minstrel’s music is indeed magical, he is not in league with ‘The Blinding Death’ as Alrik claims. Redfern shares information with the bridge guardian Athanoc. This ancient Elf knew Redfern’s grandmother when she apprenticed under Darlorhan. Redfern has heard about Ammenvale but will not betray the Sons of Asuryan. Deep down, he’s afraid to learn the truth about his grandmother.

## **Redfern’s Lute**
Redfern will share his knowledge of the ‘Lord of Shadows’ with characters who protect him from Alrik’s bounty hunters. The _War of the Beard_ section on page 4 can be used as a basis for Redfern’s story. He doesn’t know about Darlorhan’s Nurglish corruption. Although Redfern suspects a coverup of some sort by the cult of Asuryan, he only confesses this to Eonir characters who’ve earned his trust. After guiding characters to Kor Immarmor, Redfern is inclined to return to the Golden Wood. 

The Lute Redfern carries is well made, but for much of its existence was otherwise unremarkable. After a particularly stirring performance in the Golden Wood some years ago, a forest spirit was so entranced by Redfern’s music that it took up residence inside his lute. By playing, Redfern can coax the spirit into casting any spell from the Lore of Life with a  CN of 6 or less as if it had made the Casting Test with 0 SL to spare. In anyone else’s hands, it is likely the spirit would flee and the lute become inert. 

## **Athanoc**
## **Guardian Mage of the Laurelorn**
Athanoc is one of Laurelorn’s few surviving refugees from the War of the Beard. He arrived from Kor Vanaeth (now Altdorf) and lived with other refugees in the riverside caves. In that era, the bridge was made of stone. Athanoc is now a hermit with few ties. The dour guardian wears brown furs over grey robes and carries a staff of Lornalim. He is bored of gatekeeping but doesn’t trust anyone else with the responsibility. 

## **Engidu**
## **Ancient of the Underwood**
Engidu is an ancient being, possessed of abilities and motivations alien even to the Elves who know him best. He does not have a profile, but can can manifest as a Treekin (page 40) should he wish. If the Characters attempt to fight Engidu while he appears as a Treekin, he may entertain the effort for a round or two before abandoning his unfortunate host. He will take revenge  in inventive and long lasting ways. For example, he may ask the sprit of the Demst river to ensure its waters never again slake the thirst of any who attacked him, or invoke ancient pacts to ensure that wood from the Laurelorn crumbles to ash at the victims touch. One  need only consider that such timbers are used in buildings, weapons, and boats across the Empire to realise the inconvenience this might cause. Breaking such a curse might be an adventure in its own right.

## **Sons of Asuryan**
The Sons of Asuryan consist of 42 elite warriors who’ve devoted their lives to Asuryan’s plan. Half of their number are currently based in Ammenvale and Kor Immarmor. The remainder guard Asuryan’s temple in Tor Lithanel or patrol other arcane sites throughout the Laurelorn. Keeper patrols traditionally include seven Sons of Asuryan (or ‘ _Aesasur_ ’) who are proficient with bow and glaive. Initiation requires swearing an oath to the Phoenix King. 

The Queen of Laurelorn recognises the group’s legacy but secretly considers them potential traitors to the Eonir. Without guidance from the seers of Lileath, the Sons have turned to the voice of Darlorhan for instruction. Over time, the cult has become increasingly patriarchal. Its members remain unaware that Darlorhan is a puppet of Nurgle. Sons of Asuryan rarely speak, favouring hand signals to communicate with one another. Verbal negotiation with trespassers is handled by the patrol leader, and is usually brief.

## **Herr Oswald Kochler, Forester Guildmaster**
Herr Kochler is a prominent timber merchant and Salzenmund city councillor, who owns logging camps near the Laurelorn village of Vesterrup. He recently founded the Nordland Foresters’ Guild to represent woodsmen and protest logging quotas imposed by Elves. Kochler is not above working with Goblins to arrange a lucrative deal. While touring the Laurelorn to spread misinformation and advocate anti-Elf policies, Kochler is escorted by a band of sycophantic woodsmen with axes to grind. 

Nurgle’s favour was bestowed upon the merchant years prior to the current outbreak. The sickness left Kochler with bald patches in his curly black hair, which he covers by wearing a large, gaudy hat. His skin is pale and clammy, and he frequently rubs his hands together as if anticipating something. Herr Kochler spreads misinformation about the plague to incriminate Eonir and cause a wider conflict in the Laurelorn. Suitably articulate foresters are inducted into Kochler’s cult with a ‘golden handshake’ that makes recipients immune to Eyeslime Fever, but also begins a process of internal rot.

## **The Olly Axemen J**
The Nordland Foresters’ Guild has already surpassed a hundred members. Most of them are woodsmen and hunters who were raised from childhood to fear Elves. Guildmaster Kochler hand-picks the most articulate foresters for his personal clique which he calls “the jolly axemen”. These rugged frontiersmen make fine cultists of Nurgle because their personalities are jovial on the outside but hateful on the inside. The guild also includes a dozen or so sawmill workers and timber merchants. 

The Jolly Axemen are blissfully unaware that they serve Nurgle because Herr Kochler’s ‘golden handshake’ gives them immunity to Eyeslime Fever. They appear hale and hearty with full heads of hair. However, Jolly Axemen are vectors for corruption of another kind. While Chaos taint slowly consumes their souls, the cultists spread messages of hate and violence in the Laurelorn. The resultant confusion and turmoil ultimately leads to more sickness and spawns new forms of contagion.

## **Mulch-Rot, Herald of Grubile**
The Plaguebearer that brought Eyeslime Fever is a grotesque pot-bellied cyclops covered in fungal cysts. Mulch-Rot was birthed from the mournful souls of drowning swamp trees. In the mortal realm, Mulch-Rot possesses the husks of trees, whichs begin to rot within days and grow thick patches of mold. Other Plaguebearers gather around scraping eagerly at MulchRot’s mold to spread the infection. 

Mulch-Rot’s daemonic underlings cannot venture far from Ammenvale without losing stability, but Maddened Spites in the vicinity spread their mold spores. Grubile’s herald is more resilient, having ventured as far as Vesterrup to deliver the fever. On these excursions, Mulch-Rot spreads Grubile’s spores and corrupts new Spites to the service of Nurgle. Human cultists do not require guidance from Mulch-Rot, because the mortal Oswald Kochler is unnaturally gifted in Chaotic demagoguery.

## New Creature Trait: Flammable
This creature is particularly susceptible to damage from fire. If an attack or effect that strikes this creature has a chance to give it an Ablaze condition there is no need for any Test, it simply does. If this creature would lose any Wounds due to an Ablaze condition, the amount is doubled. 

## **Tree Kin**
In the Laurelorn forest, incorporeal spirits of various kinds inhabit the husks of dead trees. These animated hulks with branches for limbs are a parody of humanoids. Nature spirits possess trees temporarily to fight intruders. Should these Tree Kin be slain, the dispersed nature spirits may survive. Another type of Tree Kin is the soul vessel, created by Eonir (Forestborn) funeral rites to shelter departed Elven souls from Chaos. Soul vessels are normally inanimate but can be awakened by magic or damage. Preserved Elven souls are mere shadows of their former selves that disappear into the Aethyr when the Tree Kin is slain.

## **Maddened Tree Kin**
Though Grubile has yet to find a means to truly grant Nurgle’s gifts to the Tree Kin of the Laurelorn, this is not for want of trying, and his herald has had some limited success. MulchRot has infested several Tree Kin with parasites, vermin, and other small creatures infused with Nurgle’s vile influence. Their incessant scratching, vomitus expulsions, and horrendous screeching has left these unfortunate beings bereft of their senses. They know only that their forest is under attack, though not from whom. Mulch-Rot appears to these Maddened Tree Kin as one of their own and will set them upon any trespassers who would meddle with his master’s plans.

## **Spites**
Certain nature spirits of the Laurelorn are substantial enough that they cause magical energy to solidify, allowing them to manifest physically. Spites are diverse in appearance and ability. Common forms include glowing marshlights, miniature winged elves and thorny stick-people. Occasionally, Spites ride birds or large flying insects. These tiny creatures gather in numbers, usually near Treemen, Tree Kin or Dryads. Spites are capricious in temperament, but they can develop affinities for Wood Elves and some human Hedgefolk. When Spites are killed their bodies dissolve and their spirits return whence they came. As a result, they can only be examined closely if captured alive.

## **Maddened Spites**
Under normal circumstnaces Spites are dangerous and capricious, spirits of wild nature with no love for mortals, whose civilisations encroach upon their habitats. The influence of Nurgle on the region around Ammenvale has had a deleterious effect on many of the Spites that live there, and whilst they have not become corrupted in the sense that followers of Chaos are, they have grown increasingly hostile, and vectors of infection. The Maddened Spites found in the tainted wood look like bloated insects, often bees, coated in a fine dusting of red mould. Those who look closely will see the creatures bear twisted, Elflike faces beneath their long, curling antennae. These nocturnal spirits spread Eyeslime Fever by passing the Red Blight to new trees around Nordland villages. Some Humans and Dwarfs have begun to associate them with the plague.

## **Selling Medicine**
Traders can sell plague medicine at the Market Towns circled on the map. Selling medicine can be treated as an Endeavour ( _**WFRP,**_ page 195) that’s performed during pauses in the action (e.g. after leaving the Golden Wood or Ammenvale). Characters can split up to sell at different Market Towns during this downtime or choose a different Endeavour. Medicine can also be sold during regular gameplay when the party visits a Market Town together. 

**1. Check for Demand:** Roll against Demand % to determine if a local buyer is found. 

**2. Haggle for Price:** Seller decides asking price/dose. A **Haggle** Test is required if higher than the listed matrix price (maximum +25%). 

**3. Close the Deal:** Traders can sell 2d10 doses of each herb per Endeavour (or 4d10 doses in large cities). 

Distributing medicine is important for saving lives. Characters can always give away medicine for which they cannot find buyers. After an Endeavour, the party may regroup at a previously agreed adventure location to resume the scenario.

## Market Towns
Keen traders will wish to find out where a medicine earns the most profit. This is a **Challenging (+0) Gossip** Test, as everyone is open to discussing the availability of medicine. The accuracy with which Demand and Price are discerned depends on SL, while failure might see Characters fed entirely false information. Medicine can be sold at smaller villages, but only in single doses, and for half the price of the nearest Market Town. 

## Zelebhorn
Zelebhorn is currently the site of a military checkpoint and isolation camp. Nordland and Middenland soldiers inspect travellers for symptoms, turning back any who display them. Southbound travellers are redirected to the isolation camp where they must remain for 3 days without symptoms. The town’s sawmills are closed because of the plague. Two Jolly Axemen (page 10) loiter about promoting bogus cures and teaching antiElven slurs to idle mill workers. 

The isolation camp has turned Zelebhorn into a market town for plague medicine. Some of the wealthy travellers confined here will even pay for unproven cures. There are more charlatans in the camp than genuine physicians. The local tailor earns a tidy profit selling masks for 5/- and gloves for 4/- a pair. 

## Hargendorf
This walled port town is the capital of the Barony of Hargenfels. Townsfolk welcome Eonir traders and tolerate religious diversity, however the plague has forced Hargendorf into lockdown. Outside the gate is a bustling herb market and a quarantine camp. A pair of exhausted Shallyan nuns assist the renowned physician, Doktor Greiss. The herb market is operated by a smuggling ring connected with the Hargenfels family. 

Doktor Greiss is a busy man of science with no patience for quack medicine. He will describe Laurelorn Fever’s symptoms and treatments (page 33) to anyone who brings him Moonflower. While buying Moonflower in the Forstmark last week, he was chased away by Foresters’ Guild thugs. The Shallyan mission that ventured south to find a cure has not yet returned. 

## Skogholm
The smaller of the two Nikse border fortresses was constructed by Dwarf masons and is maintained by their descendants. Inside the fort is a village of low houses with extensive underground quarters. Secret tunnels extend for miles beneath the forest into the Elven wood. Alrik Okrisson lives in Skogholm but currently operates his bounty hunting network from Forstfast. Wood Elves are planning a retaliatory attack on Skogholm in Alrik’s absence. Skogholm is under quarantine because its Dwarf population has been devastated by the plague. Nearly fifty Dwarf deaths have spurred the demand for plague medicine, and the Dwarfs have enough gold stashed away to pay for it. The medicine market is brokered by a superstitious apothecary named Mordrek who constantly makes warding signs and mutters prayers to Grungni. 

## Market Cities
After the adventure, even better profits can be made at Salzenmund or Middenheim if a trader belongs to a relevant guild (Merchants, Apothecaries, or Physicians).
